name: Toulmin Argument
summary: Build a rigorous case: claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier and rebuttal, so the audience can test every link.
references: Stephen Toulmin, The Uses of Argument (1958)
title_style: Action titles: each title is a full sentence stating the slide's conclusion, under 15 words.

sequence.purpose: Grounds: the facts behind the claim.
Warrant: why the grounds support the claim.
Backing: support for the warrant itself.
Qualifier and rebuttal: limits and counterarguments.

pitfalls: Skipping the warrant, leaving the link between data and claim implied.
An unqualified claim that overreaches the grounds.

example.topic: A fictional research lab rescheduling its test queue
outline: Should our lab move all tests to the night queue?
Claim: moving long tests to night halves daytime waits
Grounds: 70% of daytime queue time is long tests
Warrant: removing long jobs frees the queue for short ones
Backing: synthetic replay of last month confirms it
Unless urgent fixes need long tests by day; keep a fast lane
Move long tests to night, with one daytime fast lane
